Includes marks, browsing and first encounters, formal reviews, weak-word evidence, settings, selected words, group and shuffle positions, and targets.

Restore rules:
• Timestamped marks use the newer state; choose how to resolve older marks in the preview.
• Browsing counts and latest times use the larger value; daily records are deduplicated.
• First encounters use the earlier date; reviews and weak states use the newer state. Missing old weak data keeps local data.
• Settings, selected groups and positions import only when restoring settings is selected.

Older backups without settings retain current settings. A local pre-import snapshot can undo the latest import, including any study done afterwards. Unfinished batches are not transferred and are rescheduled. Records for absent words are retained.

名：名词\n代：代词\nイ形：い形容词\nナ形：な形容词\n自動：自动词，不直接:
Source labels and their meanings:
名: noun · 代: pronoun
イ形: i-adjective · ナ形: na-adjective
自動: intransitive verb (no direct object)
他動: transitive verb (can take a direct object)
自他動: both intransitive and transitive uses

Verb classes in the source deck:
1: godan (group 1)
2: ichidan (group 2)
3: irregular, including suru and kuru

他動1 means transitive godan.
名・自動3 means a noun also used as an intransitive suru verb.

副: adverb · 連体: prenominal modifier
接: conjunction · 接頭/接尾: prefix/suffix
感: interjection · 連語/成句: expression/idiom
造: word-forming element

⓪①② etc. indicate pitch accent, not verb class. Labels follow the source deck; usage depends on the particular sense and context.

English abbreviations: n. = noun; pron. = pronoun; vi. = intransitive verb; vt. = transitive verb; adv. = adverb; i-adj. / na-adj. = i- / na-adjective. Godan and ichidan identify verb conjugation classes.

平假名和片假名表示同一套声音。平假名常见于语法和日语词汇，片假名常见于外来词等。:
Hiragana and katakana represent the same sound system. Hiragana is common in grammar and Japanese vocabulary; katakana is often used for loanwords. Start with basic kana, then voiced sounds and combinations.

The five vowels a, i, u, e, o correspond to あいうえお. Romanization is a reading aid, not English spelling. Listen and imitate Japanese pronunciation.

There are 46 basic kana. Blank cells are intentional. を is usually pronounced o as a particle; wo also identifies its spelling. ん is the moraic nasal and takes one beat (mora).

゛ marks voiced sounds (か→が); ゜ marks semi-voiced sounds (は→ぱ). In modern standard Japanese, ぢ/じ and づ/ず are generally pronounced alike, respectively.

Small ゃゅょ combine with the preceding kana into one mora: きゃ kya. Full-size きや ki-ya takes two morae.

Small っ/ッ marks a geminate consonant: hold the next consonant for an extra mora, as in きって kitte. Do not pronounce a full つ tsu.

Long vowels take an extra mora: おばさん and おばあさん are different words. Katakana often uses ー, as in コーヒー. Hiragana spellings include ああ, いい, うう, えい and おう; learn pronunciation with each word.

Particles: は→wa, へ→e, を→o. Elsewhere these kana generally have their usual readings.

This is an introductory reference, not a complete pronunciation course or stroke-order guide. Isolated-kana TTS can differ from a human demonstration.
小假名与前一个假名一起读，合计一拍。: Small kana combine with the preceding kana into one mora.
圈号表示基本音型中下降的位置，按拍计算，不是重音大小。⓪ 表示没有标记的下降；①: Circled numbers mark the downstep position in the basic pitch pattern, counted in morae, not stress intensity. ⓪ has no marked downstep; ① drops after mora 1, ② after mora 2, and so on.
きゃ 等拗音组合算一拍；っ、ん、长音各占一拍。图中附上通用助词位置，便于区别平板: Combinations such as きゃ count as one mora; っ, ん and long vowels each count as one. A following particle helps distinguish flat from word-final downstep. These are basic pitch sketches: connected speech, conjugation and dialect may differ, and TTS may not reproduce the source pattern precisely.

浏览、熟悉和正式复习是三回事: Browsing, familiar marks, and formal review are different
浏览只记录你接触过哪些词，不会自动安排到期复习。手动「熟悉」是你自己的筛选标记，: Browsing records which words you have encountered; it does not automatically schedule reviews. A manual “familiar” mark is your own filter and does not change formal review times. A word enters formal study when you first rate it in a formal task.
今日任务怎样选词？: How are words chosen for today’s task?
先取当前范围内已经到期的正式复习词，再用当天剩余的新学额度补新词。新词可以是你尚:
The task takes formally studied words that are due in the current selection first, then adds new words within today’s remaining new-word allowance. New words may include words you have not browsed yet.

For example, with a daily target of 10 new words, a batch of 20, 12 due words, and no new words formally studied today, the first round can contain 12 old words plus 8 new ones. A later round can add at most 2 more new words, while still prioritizing words that are due at that time.

每日新学目标只限制当天第一次正式评分的新词，不限制旧词复习。每批词数控制这一轮先: The daily new-word target limits only words rated formally for the first time that day; it does not limit review of old words. Batch size sets how many distinct words to schedule at the start of one round. Choose a preset or any whole number from 1 to 50; changes affect only newly scheduled rounds. Fixed browsing groups and “skip familiar words” do not reduce formal tasks. Level, frequency, study source, and custom word selection still apply.
三个评分会怎样安排？: What do the three ratings do?
没想起：约1分钟后到期。\n模糊：约10分钟后到期。\n记得：按阶段逐步延长，通:
Forgot: due in about 1 minute.
Unsure: due in about 10 minutes.
Remembered: the interval grows by stage, usually 1, 3, 7, 14, then 30 days.

If you answer correctly soon after forgetting, the app first checks again in about 10 minutes rather than treating the word as securely remembered. These are the app’s existing simple interval rules, not a guarantee of permanent mastery.

Repeats within a round and formal due times are handled separately. Ratings save immediately. Skipping submits no rating and does not count as completion. You can resume after leaving; abandoning a round does not undo saved ratings.
